```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(ggplot2); library(DT) })
P  <- "/project/xinhe/xsun/GLI-Hedgehog_Signaling"
r  <- read.delim(file.path(P, "results/1.geneset_enrichment/enrichment_fisher.tsv"), check.names = FALSE)
set_order <- c("TADA-high_fu2022", "TADA-med_fu2022", "TADA-high&med_fu2022", "NDD_wang2022",
               "SFARI_cat1", "SFARI_cat2", "SFARI_cat1&2")
bg_lab <- c(protein_coding = "vs all protein-coding genes", clustered = "vs the other 9 clusters")
r$gene_set   <- factor(r$gene_set, set_order)
r$bg         <- factor(bg_lab[r$background], bg_lab)
rc <- r[r$cluster != "all", ]
rc$cluster_f <- factor(rc$cluster, rev(as.character(1:10)))   # cluster 1 on top
pick <- function(b, k, s, v) r[r$background == b & r$cluster == k & r$gene_set == s, v]
f2  <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)

# chart ink and diverging pair (blue = depleted, gray = no change, red = enriched)
INK <- "#0b0b0b"; INK2 <- "#52514e"; MUTED <- "#898781"; GRID <- "#e1e0d9"; AXIS <- "#c3c2b7"
SURF <- "#fcfcfb"; BLUE <- "#2a78d6"; RED <- "#e34948"; MID <- "#f0efec"; ORANGE <- "#eb6834"
th <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), plot.background = element_rect(fill = SURF, colour = NA),
        strip.text = element_text(colour = INK, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = INK2), axis.title = element_text(colour = INK2),
        legend.title = element_text(colour = INK2), legend.text = element_text(colour = INK2),
        plot.caption = element_text(colour = MUTED, hjust = 0))
```

**Test:** Fisher's exact test, two-sided, on each of the 10 clusters &times;
7 gene sets, against two backgrounds. Definitions are on the
[overview](overview.html) and [gene sets](gene_sets.html) pages. FDR is
Benjamini–Hochberg within each background.

# Summary

```{r summary_numbers}
s  <- rc[rc$fdr < 0.05, ]
c6 <- function(set, b = "protein_coding") pick(b, "6", set, c("overlap", "expected", "fold", "fdr"))
t6h <- c6("TADA-high_fu2022"); t6m <- c6("TADA-med_fu2022")
t6hc <- c6("TADA-high_fu2022", "clustered")
```

* **Cluster 6 is the main signal.** It is enriched for all 7 gene sets, against
  both backgrounds. TADA-high genes: `r t6h$overlap` observed vs
  `r f2(t6h$expected)` expected (`r f2(t6h$fold)`&times; vs the genome;
  `r f2(t6hc$fold)`&times; vs the other clusters). Enrichment is stronger for
  TADA-high (`r f2(t6h$fold)`&times;) than TADA-med (`r f2(t6m$fold)`&times;),
  the pattern expected if the signal is real.
* **Cluster 2** is enriched for NDD and SFARI category 1 genes;
  **cluster 1** for SFARI category 2. Neither is significant for TADA.
* **Cluster 5 is depleted** relative to the other clusters: about half the
  expected number of SFARI and NDD genes.
* Pooling all clusters, GLI-responsive genes are enriched for every gene set
  relative to the genome (fold `r f2(min(r$fold[r$cluster == "all"]))`–`r f2(max(r$fold[r$cluster == "all"]))`).
  This may partly reflect that genes expressed in neural progenitors are
  generally NDD-enriched, which is why the second background matters.
* In total, `r sum(s$direction == "enriched")` cluster tests are significantly
  enriched and `r sum(s$direction == "depleted")` depleted (FDR < 0.05).

# Fold enrichment, all clusters and gene sets

```{r heatmap, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.6}
h <- rc
h$l2 <- pmax(pmin(log2(h$fold), 2), -2)        # fold 0 (no overlap) shows as the darkest blue
h$lab <- ifelse(h$fdr < 0.05, f2(h$fold), "")
h$lab_col <- ifelse(abs(h$l2) > 1.1, "#ffffff", INK)
h$alpha <- ifelse(h$fdr < 0.05, 1, 0.35)        # fade non-significant cells
ggplot(h, aes(gene_set, cluster_f, fill = l2)) +
  geom_tile(aes(alpha = alpha), colour = SURF, linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_alpha_identity() +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab, colour = lab_col), size = 3.3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = BLUE, mid = MID, high = RED, midpoint = 0, limits = c(-2, 2),
                       breaks = log2(c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4)), labels = c("≤0.25", "0.5", "1", "2", "≥4"),
                       name = "Fold\n(observed /\nexpected)") +
  facet_wrap(~ bg) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cluster",
       caption = paste("Red = enriched, blue = depleted. Solid cells with numbers: FDR < 0.05 (BH within each background);",
                       "faded cells: not significant. Fold 0 (no overlap) shows as the darkest blue.")) +
  th + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1), legend.key.height = unit(14, "pt"))
```

# Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals

Each point is one cluster. A filled point means FDR < 0.05; a hollow one is
not significant. Clusters with no overlap (odds ratio 0) are drawn at the left
edge.

```{r forest, fig.width=11, fig.height=7.2}
fp <- rc
lo <- 0.05; hi <- 20
fp$or <- pmin(pmax(fp$odds_ratio, lo), hi)
fp$cl <- pmax(fp$ci_low, lo); fp$ch <- pmin(fp$ci_high, hi)
fp$sig <- fp$fdr < 0.05
ggplot(fp, aes(or, cluster_f, colour = bg, group = bg)) +   # group = bg keeps dodge order fixed
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = AXIS, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = cl, xmax = ch), height = 0, linewidth = 0.6,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = ifelse(sig, as.character(bg), "none")), shape = 21, size = 2.6, stroke = 0.9,
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(BLUE, ORANGE), bg_lab), name = "Background") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(setNames(c(BLUE, ORANGE), bg_lab), none = SURF), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10(limits = c(lo, hi), breaks = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 10), labels = c("0.1", "0.25", "0.5", "1", "2", "4", "10")) +
  facet_wrap(~ gene_set, ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Odds ratio (log scale)", y = "Cluster") +
  th + theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = GRID, linewidth = 0.3),
             legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left")
```

# Pooled: all clustered genes vs the genome

```{r pooled}
a <- r[r$cluster == "all", ]
a <- a[order(a$gene_set), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(a$gene_set, a$n_set, a$overlap, f2(a$expected), sprintf("%.2f", a$fold),
                        sprintf("%.2f", a$odds_ratio), signif(a$fdr, 2)),
             col.names = c("Gene set", "Set size", "In clustered genes", "Expected", "Fold", "Odds ratio", "FDR"))
```

# Cluster 6: overlapping genes

```{r c6genes}
g6 <- r[r$background == "protein_coding" & r$cluster == "6", ]
g6 <- g6[order(g6$gene_set), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(g6$gene_set, g6$overlap, gsub(",", ", ", g6$overlap_genes)),
             col.names = c("Gene set", "Genes", "Overlapping genes"))
```

# Full results table

All 147 tests (`results/1.geneset_enrichment/enrichment_fisher.tsv`). Use the
search boxes to filter.

```{r table}
tt <- r[, c("background", "cluster", "gene_set", "n_cluster", "n_set", "overlap", "expected",
            "fold", "odds_ratio", "ci_low", "ci_high", "direction", "p_value", "fdr", "overlap_genes")]
for (v in c("fold", "odds_ratio", "ci_low", "ci_high")) tt[[v]] <- round(tt[[v]], 2)
for (v in c("p_value", "fdr")) tt[[v]] <- signif(tt[[v]], 3)
datatable(tt, filter = "top", rownames = FALSE,
          options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE,
                         columnDefs = list(list(targets = ncol(tt) - 1, width = "300px"))))
```

# Caveats

* The genome-wide background includes genes not expressed in these cells.
  The "other clusters" background is stricter, but asks a different question
  (cluster vs other GLI-responsive genes).
* Cluster 6 is the largest cluster (`r pick("protein_coding", "6", "SFARI_cat1", "n_cluster")`
  genes), which gives it the most power.
* The gene sets overlap heavily, so the 7 results per cluster are not
  independent findings.
* Not yet done: DD-specific list, confidence-tier comparisons for NDD, and a
  test that accounts for mutation-intolerant genes.
